thread:
opsbot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT: streaming-api eu-central-1 - elevated 503s and streaming connection resets. Pager escalation sent to on-call.

alex: saw the page, I'm primary for the night. quick summary: 503 rate jumped ~12:10 UTC, primarily in eu-central streaming endpoints (streaming.start / stream.connect). Latency also spiking for some requests. No broad infra alert besides app errors. Investigating autoscaler and sidecar failures.

sana: I'm secondary. joining. any customer-facing impact yet?

alex: two paying customers reported session drops (OAuth flows) — CS DM'd logs. We've temporarily routed some VIP traffic to us-east as a stopgap. Will note which routes/tenants below.

liam: opsbot shows pod restarts on streaming-worker-xx in eu-central-az-b. crashlooping on worker that manages persistent-kv. Suspect a memregression from last night's runtime patch.

maria: adding runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/streaming-503 (follow the "regional surge" section). Also check /infra/autoscale/events for failed scaleups.

alex: actions taken so far:
- rolled back runtime patch on 4 nodes (eu-central-az-b) to previous tag (rtn-2026.03.07) to stop OOMs
- manual scale: requested +10 streaming-worker instances in eu-central group (pending cloud confirmations)
- added temporary route to us-east for tenants: tenant-acme, tenant-aurora (see routing table update)
- paused canary rollout of 2026.03.08 runtime across streaming fleet

sana: current mitigations in progress:
- cloud team verifying instance spin-up; ETA ~6-8 min
- infra to restart sidecar-proxy on restarted pods to clear conn tracking
- golden metrics to watch: streaming_503_rate, streaming_conn_resets, pod_oom_count

dylan: i'm watching logs. I'm seeing repeated ``ERR conn reset by peer`` in worker logs followed by ``panic: kvcache nil deref`` on a subset. suspect regression in kvcache Null handling.

alex: good catch. morris (eng-ml) commented in repo yesterday about a change. we're reverting that tomorrow if this stabilizes.

liam: cloud console shows 6/10 requested instances started, 4 still provisioning. Autoscaler had 3 failed attempts due to instance quota in eu-central; raised support ticket to cloud provider (ticket #CP-5421).

maria: customer impact note for handoff:
- severity: partial (some streaming sessions dropped; API fallbacks to polling for affected customers)
- regions impacted: eu-central primarily, minor traffic affected in eu-west
- affected customers: tenant-acme (high), tenant-aurora (medium), a couple small customers with webhooks (low)
- suggested comms: tell CS to message impacted customers with "temporary degraded streaming" and that we're rerouting / scaling. no ETA yet.

sana: monitoring checklist for next shift:
- confirm cloud requested instances reached 100% healthy
- watch streaming_503_rate < 0.5% for 30m before un-routing to us-east
- confirm no OOMs from runtime rollback
- ensure canary rollout remains paused (don't resume)
- escalate to oncall ENG-LEAD if customer-acme still above 5% session drop after 1h

alex: run commands for next on-call (copy/paste):
```
# check 503 rate (PromQL)
sum(rate(streaming_http_responses{code="503",region="eu-central"}[5m])) by (region)

# tail logs for crashes
kubectl -n prod logs -l app=streaming-worker -c runtime --since=10m | grep -i "panic\|oom\|kvcache"

# check autoscaler events
gcloud compute instance-groups managed list-instances streaming-eu-central
```

dylan: note: if you hit repeated kvcache panics, do NOT restart the whole pool at once. Restart in batches of 3 and monitor.

liam: cloud provider updated ticket: added quota bump request, advised to use spare capacity in eu-west if provisioning stalls >20m. I've authorized fallback allocation to eu-west as second step.

sana: outstanding items for next team:
- confirm ticket CP-5421 outcome
- confirm rollback stability for 60m
- keep routing for tenant-acme to us-east until 30m stable window
- prep incident timeline for postmortem (I'll draft during my shift)

alex: handoff summary — primary->sana (taking next 4h). secondary->liam. on-call lead for escalation is maria.

sana: I'll take over now. flagging a small coverage gap from 02:00-03:00 UTC (on-call rotation hasn't scheduled a backup). tagging @maria to confirm coverage.

maria: I can cover that gap. adding myself to rotation for 02:00-03:30 UTC. :thumbsup:

opsbot: NOTE: page acknowledged by alex and sana. All future pages consolidated into this thread. Incident state: mitigation-in-progress -> partial-mitigation

alex: leaving the bridge. Sana, I put my notes in the incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-412. Good luck.

sana: got it. taking over and will ping here with updates every 15-30m or on any major change. if you need me immediately: @sana
